abstract: This study examines the growth and cyclical effects of energy using annual data from Fiji over the period 1980 to 2021. Drawing insights from the post-Keynesian demand-led growth framework, the study finds negative energy shocks reduce output more strongly in expansions compared to how positive energy shocks increase output in recessions. Positive energy shocks and negative energy shocks do not impact GDP in expansions, and recessions, respectively. The results are robust to alternative cyclical decomposition filters and structural breaks through the Fourier NARDL model. Moreover, the Fourier-based Granger causality test results indicate unidirectional causality from energy to growth. The results underscore the role of energy to support growth in expansion, albeit highlighting bottlenecks in production. The results indicate that due to weak demand, declines in energy do not further depress output in recessions. Policymakers may use the findings to benefit from energy’s economic effects whilst mitigating climate risks.
authors: Nikeel Nishkar Kumar Manu Sharma a School of Economics, Finance, and Marketing
title: Nonlinear growth and cyclical effects of energy: evidence from Fiji with a Fourier NARDL model
title_zh: 斐济能源的非线性增长与周期效应：基于傅里叶非线性自回归分布滞后模型的证据

abstract: This paper empirically tests whether Rolex watches may be considered safe-haven assets. To accomplish this, we employ Local Gaussian Correlations and spectral analysis spanning from 19 January 2017 to 7 July 2023, examining the relationship between the Rolex market index (indicating the average market price of the watches) and more conventional assets, namely: S&P 500, Oil, Nikkei, Eurostoxx, Gold, REIT, EEM and Bitcoin. The results revealed that the Rolex market index, and hence Rolex watches, exhibited safe-haven properties during the pandemic crisis in the majority of the cases (except for Gold and REIT). This finding is vital for global investors since the identified safe-haven features might help enhance portfolio diversification strategies in anticipation of future crises.
abstract_zh: 本文实证检验了劳力士手表是否可被视为避险资产。为此，我们采用局部高斯相关性和谱分析方法，研究时间跨度自2017年1月19日至2023年7月7日，考察劳力士市场指数（反映手表平均市场价格）与更传统资产之间的关系，这些资产包括：标普500指数、石油、日经指数、欧洲斯托克指数、黄金、房地产投资信托基金、新兴市场指数及比特币。结果显示，在疫情期间，劳力士市场指数及其所代表的劳力士手表在多数情况下展现出避险属性（黄金和房地产投资信托基金除外）。这一发现对全球投资者至关重要，因为识别出的避险特征可能有助于在未来危机前优化投资组合多元化策略。
authors: Dimitrios Dimitriou Georgios Garafas Dimitris Kenourgios Alexandros Tsioutsios a Department of Accounting and Finance

School of Economics and Political Sciences

title: A new elite safe haven asset: Rolex watches
title_zh: 新的精英避险资产：劳力士手表
